A Russian scientist, poet and scholar, born to a fisherman's family near Arkhangelsk on the White Sea in 1711. He died in Saint Petersburg in 1765.

At nineteen he walked to Moscow to study, hiding his peasant birth. He was sent to Germany to study chemistry and mining, and joined the new Academy of Sciences that Peter the Great had planned. He worked in chemistry, physics, astronomy and geology, saw that Venus has an atmosphere during its transit in 1761, and set up a glass works that made coloured mosaics.

He also shaped Russian letters. His grammar and his rules for verse helped form the modern literary language, and he wrote odes to the empresses. In 1755 he helped found Moscow University with the courtier Ivan Shuvalov. It now bears his name, as Lomonosov Moscow State University. To later Russians he was the model of a self made genius, a man from the far north who reached the top of the Enlightenment.
sum: A Russian scientist, poet and scholar, born to a fisherman's family near Arkhangelsk on the White Sea in 1711. He died in Saint Petersburg in 1765.
